source_caption:
One of the most famous and widely shared elements of The Curious Case of Benjamin Button is the emotional voiceover monologue that begins, “For what it’s worth: it’s never too late or, in my case, too early to be whoever you want to be”. Despite being tattooed, printed on inspirational posters, and endlessly circulated online with steadfast attributions to F. Scott Fitzgerald, the quote does not exist anywhere in Fitzgerald’s original 1922 short story. The entire poignant speech was actually an original creation by screenwriter Eric Roth, specifically crafted for the film to anchor the sweeping, global montage of Benjamin’s life. Roth wrote the lines to give Brad Pitt’s character a profound emotional thesis that capitalized on the narrative’s unique reverse-aging premise, resulting in one of the most widely misattributed quotes in modern cinema history.

The Curious Case of Benjamin Button (2008), directed by David Fincher, starring Brad Pitt, Cate Blanchett, Taraji P. Henson, Mahershala Ali. Born under unusual circumstances in New Orleans at the end of World War I, a man who ages in reverse navigates the complexities of life, love, and loss as he physically grows younger while the world around him grows older.

source_details.synopsis: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button is a 2008 American fantasy drama film directed by David Fincher and adapted by Eric Roth and Robin Swicord from F. Scott Fitzgerald's 1922 short story. The film stars Brad Pitt as a man who ages in reverse and Cate Blanchett as his love interest throughout his life. The film also stars Taraji P. Henson, Julia Ormond, Jason Flemyng, Elias Koteas, and Tilda Swinton. Producer Ray Stark bought the film rights to do the short story in the mid-1980s with Universal Pictures backing the film, but struggled to get the project off the ground until he sold the rights to producers Kathleen Kennedy and Frank Marshall in the 1990s.
